text:
Liam: Heads-up: AcmeEval (trial) is getting a flood of 5xxs starting ~13:34PT when they pushed a big batch job (spiky bursts ~250-320 rps). Sales on the thread, CISO asked for root cause + short-term SLA.

deploy-bot: autoscaler: scale request triggered for eval-pool-2 at 13:35:08; added 3 instances.

Priya: What status codes? 500/502/503? Any request IDs to trace?

Liam: Mostly 502 and intermittent 503. Sample request IDs: b3cf9a12, d5a4f3e7. Model: r-instruct-large-v1, batch config: tenant_default, typical payload small.

Nora: I pulled frontdoor traces. Pattern: rapid queue growth -> worker grpc error (code=14) -> frontdoor maps to 502. New instances show long model-init (~18s) because quant-kernel JIT. No OOM.

Devon: Quick fixes we can do: 1) enable tenant-level warm pool (prewarmed VM) 2) enable per-tenant burst allowance (smooth the burst into bursts/sec) 3) temporary model fallback to r-instruct-medium-quant (lower mem) when queue_threshold exceeded. Which do we want?

Liam: Sales wants the cheapest option that guarantees the demo tomorrow. Also CISO wants the diagnostic bundle and confirmation of log retention window.

Priya: For immediate demo safety: enable fallback path + reduce max_batch to 2 for that tenant; also apply short warm pool (1 GPU prewarmed) for next 12h. That should cut tail latency and prevent grpc 14.

deploy-bot: apply: set tenant(acmeeval).max_batch=2 -> accepted
deploy-bot: apply: set fallback_route(acmeeval)=r-instruct-medium-quant -> accepted

Devon: Cost note: warm instance prewarm hourly = $0.65/hr for eval-sized GPU (market price), so ~ $15.60 for 24h; if we offer hourly billing for trials we can absorb first 4h as courtesy.

Priya: I'll draft a one-paragraph quote for sales: recommend warm pool for demo window + fallback enabled. Price impact ~ $16/day (pro-rated) + marginal token cost if fallback model differs. Sending now.

Nora: Uploaded audit bundle with traces and instance boot logs: https://redwood-internal/diag/2621119876 . Bundle includes frontdoor spans, worker logs, model load timestamps, and autoscale events. Retention: default diag retention 30d; CISO can request extended retention via security@redwood.ai.

sales-bot: Noted. Sales: Acme contact wants reassurance. Can we give a "no 5xx" guarantee?

Devon: We can't fully guarantee zero 5xxs but with warm pool + aggressive queue-based scaling + fallback we can reduce probability dramatically. Recommend scheduling a practice run at the demo hour with traffic replay.

Priya: Operational plan I emailed sales: (1) enable warm pool for 12h starting now, (2) fallback enabled, (3) temporary scale_policy=queue-based with cooldown lowered to 30s for the eval-pool, (4) client-side retries 2x with jitter.

Liam: Client retry snippet I gave them earlier: 
```
POST /v1/generate
Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN
{
  "model": "r-instruct-large-v1",
  "max_tokens": 128,
  "batch_size": 1
}
```
Add exponential backoff: base=100ms, max=1s.

deploy-bot: apply: eval-pool-2.scale_policy=queue_based cooldown=30s duration=12h -> accepted

Nora: Monitoring: queue_depth peaked at 320; after policy flip and fallback we see successful drain. Current 5xx rate down from 12% -> 0.9% over 5m.

Devon: Follow-ups: (a) consider persistent warm pools for top-tier trials, (b) add a prewarm hook for quantized kernels to shave init by ~12s, (c) document pricing for prewarm in trial playbook.

Priya: I'll add legal loop for CISO if they ask for retention SLA. Also adding an ops runbook entry for tenant-fallback config.

Liam: Thanks team. Sales: I've updated Acme and scheduled a practice run at demo time. Will escalate if anything spikes. :thumbsup:

Nora: I'll keep the diagnostic link pinned to the sales thread and post final confirmation 30m before demo.

Devon: Closing: current health ok. Will revert temporary configs after 12h unless sales asks to extend.

Priya: Noted.

Liam: Good work, everyone.
